title: Environmental Cooperation: Design and Implementation
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
Many environmental systems cross borders. An atmosphere protected by one country can still be damaged by emissions elsewhere, while the benefits of protection are widely shared. This creates a collective-action problem: every government may prefer a stable environment, yet each may hope that others pay more of the cost. A declaration of common concern identifies the problem but does not change those incentives by itself.

International cooperation therefore needs an architecture. Scientists must develop measurements and explain uncertainty. Governments must define controlled activities, reporting rules, review, finance, and procedures for revising commitments. Domestic institutions must then change permits, investment, enforcement, and technology. The chain can fail at any link; a signed agreement is neither nothing nor the completed environmental outcome.

The Montreal Protocol illustrates several useful mechanisms. It targeted a defined group of ozone-depleting substances, used schedules that could be strengthened as evidence changed, and combined controls with support for implementation. Production and consumption of many controlled substances fell sharply, and scientific assessments indicate ozone recovery is under way. Success came from science, substitution, monitoring, finance, industry response, and repeated adjustment—not from diplomatic language alone.

Climate change differs in scale and structure. Greenhouse gases arise across energy, transport, buildings, industry, agriculture, and land use; substitutes and transition costs vary. Countries also differ in historical emissions, capacity, development needs, and vulnerability. Lessons can transfer at the level of design—measurement, review, finance, technology, increasing ambition—but not as a promise that identical rules will produce identical speed. Cooperation must be environmentally effective and politically durable, which makes fairness part of implementation rather than an optional moral appendix.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Declaring common concern automatically changes national incentives.

options.label: B
options.text: Every environmental problem can be solved with identical rules and timing.

options.label: C
options.text: Effective cooperation connects science, treaty design, domestic implementation, adjustment, and fair burden sharing.

options.label: D
options.text: A signed agreement has no value unless the environmental problem is already solved.

questions.answer: 正解：C。本文は科学、制度設計、国内履行、反復的調整、公平な負担を一つの実効性の鎖として扱います。Aは宣言の限界、Bは問題差、Dは合意の中間的価値を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why can cooperation remain insufficient even when every government prefers environmental stability?

options.label: A
options.text: Protection benefits are widely shared, so each government may hope that others bear more of the cost.

options.label: B
options.text: Environmental benefits remain entirely inside the country that pays for them.

options.label: C
options.text: Governments cannot identify any common environmental concern.

options.label: D
options.text: Declarations automatically force every country to contribute equally.

questions.answer: 正解：A。便益は広く共有される一方で費用は各国に生じるため、他国の負担へのただ乗り誘因が生まれます。B～Dは越境性と宣言だけでは誘因が変わらない点に反します。

questions.prompt: The word “architecture” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: a connected design of rules, finance, review, and implementation

options.label: B
options.text: the physical shape of a conference building

options.label: C
options.text: one isolated scientific measurement

options.label: D
options.text: a nonbinding slogan with no institutional elements

questions.answer: 正解：A。ここでは複数の制度要素が支え合う全体設計を指します。Bは文字どおりの建築、Cは一要素だけ、Dは本文が不十分とする宣言にすぎません。

questions.prompt: Which sequence best represents the chain from international agreement to environmental improvement?

options.label: A
options.text: Scientific measurement; international rules, reporting, review, and finance; domestic permits and enforcement; technological substitution; environmental monitoring

options.label: B
options.text: Diplomatic signature; immediate recovery; later measurement if convenient

options.label: C
options.text: Domestic enforcement without defined activities, reporting, or scientific evidence

options.label: D
options.text: A declaration of concern followed by no institutional or technological change

questions.answer: 正解：A。科学的測定から国際制度、国内許認可・執行、技術代替、環境指標の確認へつながる鎖です。B～Dは必要な中間段階を飛ばしています。

questions.prompt: Why does the author not attribute the Montreal Protocol's success to diplomatic language alone?

options.label: A
options.text: Defined substances, substitutes, monitoring, finance, industry response, and repeated rule adjustments translated commitments into reductions.

options.label: B
options.text: The agreement contained no controls or implementation support.

options.label: C
options.text: Ozone recovery occurred before production and consumption changed.

options.label: D
options.text: Scientific assessments and industrial changes played no role.

questions.answer: 正解：A。対象定義、代替、監視、資金、産業対応、規則更新が実際の削減を媒介しました。B～Dは本文が列挙する実施機構と因果順序を否定します。

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of schedules that can be strengthened as evidence changes?

options.label: A
options.text: Cooperation can begin under uncertainty and become stricter as science, technology, and cost information improve.

options.label: B
options.text: Rules never need revision after the first agreement.

options.label: C
options.text: Governments must wait for perfect information before taking any action.

options.label: D
options.text: New evidence cannot affect controlled activities or commitments.

questions.answer: 正解：A。不確実性の下で開始し、新しい科学・技術・費用情報に合わせて強化できます。B・Dは適応性を否定し、Cは完全情報までの待機という本文が避ける選択です。

questions.prompt: Why cannot the ozone-protection rules simply be copied unchanged for climate change?

options.label: A
options.text: Greenhouse gases span many economic sectors, and countries differ in substitutes, costs, historical emissions, capacity, development needs, and vulnerability.

options.label: B
options.text: Climate change involves only one easily replaced substance.

options.label: C
options.text: All countries have identical responsibilities, resources, and exposure.

options.label: D
options.text: Measurement, review, finance, and technology are irrelevant to climate cooperation.

questions.answer: 正解：A。排出源が多数部門に及び、代替・費用・歴史的責任・能力・開発需要・脆弱性が異なります。B・Cは複雑性を消し、Dは移転可能な設計原則を否定します。

questions.prompt: What does the statement “Fairness is part of implementation rather than an optional moral appendix” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Perceived unfairness can weaken participation, domestic approval, compliance, and long-term durability, reducing environmental effectiveness.

options.label: B
options.text: Fairness matters only after every environmental target has already been achieved.

options.label: C
options.text: Burden sharing has no effect on political support or compliance.

options.label: D
options.text: Environmental effectiveness requires ignoring differences in capacity and vulnerability.

questions.answer: 正解：A。負担が不当と見なされると参加、国内承認、遵守、長期継続が弱まり、環境効果も下がります。B～Dは公平性を実施から切り離しています。

questions.prompt: Which set of indicators would best evaluate the effectiveness of an international environmental agreement?

options.label: A
options.text: Environmental outcomes, policy adoption, compliance, delivered finance, technology deployment, independent observations, uncertainty, distributional effects, stronger commitments, and improvement against a credible baseline

options.label: B
options.text: Only the number of countries that signed the document

options.label: C
options.text: Only diplomatic statements, without measuring implementation or environmental response

options.label: D
options.text: Total spending without checking who received support or whether emissions changed

questions.answer: 正解：A。成果、政策、遵守、資金、技術、独立観測、不確実性、分配、野心強化、反実仮想基準を連結して測ります。B～Dは署名や投入だけで追加的・持続的改善を確認できません。
